Use interval notation in your answers. Use inf to represent infinity.

solution.p: The question f(x) \ge 1 is asking: For what x values, are function fs y values greater than or equal to 1? We can break down this question into two steps:

li.p: In function fs graph, identify the part(s) whose y values are greater than or equal to 1.
Identify those x values corresponding to that part(s) of the function.

solution.p: In this functions graph, the blue parts y values are greater than or equal to 1:
The corresponding x values of the blue part(s) are in {\left(-\infty ,1\right]}. In other words, to satisfy f(x) \ge 1, function fs x values need to be in {\left(-\infty ,1\right]}.

Similarly, the functions red parts y values are smaller than 1, and the corresponding x values of the red part are in {\left(1,\infty \right)}. In other words, to satisfy f(x) \lt 1, function fs x values need to be in {\left(1,\infty \right)}.
